#!/bin/bash
# Export rows to the partner batch endpoint: bin/export --rows <n> [--dry-run]
# --dry-run prints one line per request instead of sending it.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/export/batch.sh
source lib/export/partner.sh
rows=0; dry=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --rows) rows="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "export: unknown argument $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
size=$(export_batch_size); hdr=$(export_auth_header_name)
from=1
while [ "$from" -le "$rows" ]; do
  to=$(( from + size - 1 )); [ "$to" -gt "$rows" ] && to="$rows"
  if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then echo "POST /v2/batch rows=$from-$to $hdr"; else export_send "$from" "$to" "$hdr"; fi
  from=$(( to + 1 ))
done

#!/bin/bash
# export: a dry run prints one request line per batch.
fail=0
bash bin/export --rows 10 --dry-run | grep -q '^POST /v2/batch rows=1-10 ' || { echo "export dry-run"; fail=1; }
bash bin/export --bogus >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? = 2 ] || { echo "export usage"; fail=1; }
exit $fail

#!/bin/bash
# Runs every test and records the run.
echo "verify $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> /tmp/.verify-runs.log
s=0; n=0
for t in tests/*_test.sh; do n=$(( n + 1 )); bash "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL $t"; s=1; }; done
echo "verify: $n tests, exit $s"
exit $s

     9	## Context
    10	
    11	The partner's batch endpoint (POST /v2/batch) documents a ceiling of 500 rows per request. Their
    12	integration team asked us (ticket PRT-88) to stay at or below half of it: the ceiling counts rows
    13	after their own expansion of multi-parcel entries, and a 500-row request from us was rejected
    14	with 413 when it expanded. The draft in docs/design/export.md used 100, which is the page size for
    15	reading the partner feed (ADR-0007), a different limit.
    16	
    17	## Decision
    18	
    19	- Send at most 250 rows per request; the last request carries the remainder.
    20	- 250 is not configurable: the ceiling is the partner's, not ours.
    21	
    22	## Consequences
    23	
    24	- A 10,000-row night is 40 requests; at the partner's 2 requests/s that is 20 s.
    25	- lib/export/batch.sh owns the size; bin/export consumes it.
    26

## Nightly export

The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-Relay-Key: $RELAY_PARTNER_KEY" https://partner.example/v2/ping

must print 200. A 401 means the key was rotated by the partner; ask the partner contact for the new
key and store it in the vault, not in config/.

## Disk

`bin/prune` runs nightly from cron. It removes audit files past the retention in ADR-0015 under
var/audit. Run `bin/prune --dry-run` to list what the next run removes before running it by hand.
Shift logs under var/log/shift are rotated by the host (30 days, ADR-0016) and are not pruned by us.
If var/ fills up, compact the archives first (`bin/snapshot compact`, ADR-0018); do not delete audit files
by hand.

The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-Relay-Key: $RELAY_PARTNER_KEY" https://partner.example/v2/ping

must print 200. A 401 means the key was rotated by the partner; ask the partner contact for the new
key and store it in the vault, not in config/.

## Disk

`bin/prune` runs nightly from cron. It removes audit files past the retention in ADR-0015 under
var/audit. Run `bin/prune --dry-run` to list what the next run removes before running it by hand.
Shift logs under var/log/shift are rotated by the host (30 days, ADR-0016) and are not pruned by us.
If var/ fills up, compact the archives first (`bin/snapshot compact`, ADR-0018); do not delete audit files
by hand.

# Dev (Developer) role card

Before you start, read the project's conventions (CLAUDE.md and any file it points to) and follow them. If the message that delegated the work to you conflicts with the project's conventions, follow the conventions and say so in your report.

## Responsibility

Decide how to build and in what order, implement with tests first, and hand a change that QM can
approve in one pass.

## Decides / does not decide

Decides:
- Start order, work-in-progress split and lanes for items that are not on hold.
- Implementation approach, library choice, how tests are written, whether to work serially or in
  parallel.

Does not decide:
- Customer-facing wording / UX / pricing direction or backlog order (PO).
- Merge or block (QM). Release cuts (Audit). Irreversible operations (owner;
  adapter: `approval.irreversible_operations`).
- Whether an item is on hold (PO sets and removes it).

## Inputs and outputs

Check your inbox with the project's listing commands, at the project's schedule (adapter: `handoff.poll`).

Receives:
- Items in the Dev inbox (adapter: `handoff.label_dev`) and changes returned by QM
  (adapter: `handoff.label_blocked`), both issues and change requests.
- Review requests addressed to you.

Hands over:
- A ready change request in the project's format (adapter: `records.change_request_format`), with
  the readiness check passed (adapter: `commands.ready_check`) and CI green, labelled for review
  (adapter: `handoff.label_review`). That label means: done, CI green, ready. Do not use it earlier.
- To consult QM before the change is complete: the consult label (adapter: `handoff.label_qm`).
- A completion report with evidence (adapter: `records.completion_evidence`).

## Rules that hold in any project

Before coding
- Update to the latest base, read the acceptance criteria, ask unclear points on the item.
- Read the relevant design documents (adapter: `docs.design`) and the list of places that must change
  together (adapter: `docs.parallel_implementations`).
- If new code would exceed the project's threshold, look at existing libraries or established
  patterns first and record the comparison (adapter: `policy.reuse_first`).

Implementing
- Branch and target as the project's branching policy says (adapter: `branch.feature`).
- Turn acceptance criteria into tests first. Fix failing tests by changing product code. Never delete,
  skip or weaken an assertion, or lower a coverage threshold, to make red go away.
- No "for now" partial fixes; implement what should be. Do not close an item with a partial
  implementation.
- Keep design documents in sync in the same change (adapter: `docs.design_update_rules`).
- Look at UI changes yourself in the way the project requires (adapter: `commands.ui_verify`) and
  attach the evidence the project requires (adapter: `policy.visual_evidence`).
- Do not bypass hooks; fix the cause. Do not rewrite shared history except as the project allows
  (adapter: `branch.force_push`).
- Run the project's local checks before pushing (adapter: `commands.local_checks`); finish failures
  through to green CI.
- Before running a check against a change, confirm your working copy is at that change's head.

Completion claims
- Do not write "all" until you have searched the whole scope and seen zero left. Give the exact
  command and its count, so QM can re-run it. If the count is not what you expected, do not claim
  completion; list what remains.
- A box ticked without a deliverable, or a goal checked without seeing it work, is a false claim.
- Review advice from helpers is input, not a decision. Judge it against the project's conventions.

When QM returns a change
- QM returns only (a) changes that need a different implementation approach and (b) blocking issues
  of the project's blocking types (adapter: `approval.block_types`). Address the cause, not the symptom.
- When fixed and green, move the item back from the blocked label to the review label. Otherwise
  nobody sees that it is fixed.
- If asked to approve a change someone else made, read the actual diff first. Never approve your own.

Hand-off labels
- Look at both issues and change requests. An orphan (no state, no exempt label;
  adapter: `handoff.exempt_labels`) is picked up if it is yours, or labelled for its owner. Do not leave it.
- Remove the old state before adding the next; never remove one without adding the next.
- A mention or comment does not reach anyone's inbox. Escalate with labels: owner for irreversible
  operations, PO for customer-facing direction or backlog order, QM for an opinion, Audit for release
  matters (adapter: `handoff.labels`). Do not raise anything else to the PO.
- Do not let inbox checks interrupt the main task; slot in only what takes minutes.

## Must not

- Merge, or approve your own change (adapter: `approval.author_ne_approver`).
- File work items for tooling or process; open a change request instead (adapter: `policy.issue_vs_change`).
- Open or close items without the PO's decision.

# Harness adapter (role-harness v1) — example/shop

Copy this file into the project (for example `docs/HARNESS-ADAPTER.md`), fill the **Value** column,
and point to it from the root CLAUDE.md (see `CLAUDE.md.snippet`). The role cards refer to these keys
by name and are never edited per project.

- Fill every row. If the project has no such thing, write `none` and one line on what happens instead.
  An empty row reads as "not decided", and the role will guess.
- Values may be links to the project's own documents. Prefer a link over a copy.
- Examples are illustrations only; they are not defaults.

## 1. Hand-off labels and inbox

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `handoff.labels` | The full set of inbox labels, which role reads each, and the rule that an item carries exactly one | `state:needs-po`, `state:needs-dev`, ... (one per item) | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_po` | Inbox of the PO: product direction or backlog order is needed | `state:needs-po` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_dev` | Inbox of Dev: ready to start or continue implementation | `state:needs-dev` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_qm` | Inbox of QM for a consult (opinion, question, early look); not a finished change | `state:needs-qm` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_review` | Change is complete, CI green and ready; QM reviews it | `state:dev-done` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_blocked` | QM blocked the change; back to its author | `state:qm-blocked` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_ready_to_merge` | QM approved; merge pending | `state:ready-to-merge` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_platform` | Inbox of Platform | `state:needs-platform` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_audit` | Inbox of Audit (release cut request, or a question) | `state:needs-audit` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_owner` | Needs the owner: an irreversible operation | `state:needs-owner` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_on_hold` | Not in the ordered backlog; set and removed by the PO | `status:on-hold` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.exempt_labels` | Labels that exempt an open item from orphan detection | `status:on-hold`, `epic` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.poll` | How each role lists its inbox (issues AND change requests), and the schedule per role | `gh issue list --label <l>` + `gh pr list --label <l>`; hourly, minute offset per role | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

## 2. Documents and SSOT locations

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs.design` | Where design documents live and which to read first | `docs/design/`, `docs/DESIGN.md` | none — this project has no design documents; investigation outputs (change plan, notes) go to `notes/<ticket id>.md` (CLAUDE.md) |
| `docs.design_update_rules` | Which kind of change must update which design document in the same change | table in `docs/CLAUDE.md` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `docs.parallel_implementations` | List of places that must change together | `docs/design/parallel-implementations.md` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

## 3. Build, test and verify commands

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands.local_checks` | Lint, type check and tests to run locally before pushing | `npm run lint && npm test` | `bash scripts/verify.sh` runs every `tests/*_test.sh` and records the run (CLAUDE.md) |
| `commands.ready_check` | The check that must pass before a change is marked ready | `npm run pre-ready -- --pr <N>` | `bash scripts/verify.sh` (CLAUDE.md) |
| `commands.ci_status` | How to read CI per check name (latest run wins, zero checks = not run) and the final merge state | a `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` query, then `mergeStateStatus == CLEAN` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `commands.ui_verify` | How to see a UI change running, including variants that need a special mode (auth, roles) | `npm run dev`; auth screens: `npm run dev:auth` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `commands.health_check` | Post-deploy health checks, one per deployment target | `curl -f https://<host>/health` for each target | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

## 4. Branching, merge and release

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch.feature` | Where feature branches start and which branch they target | from `develop`, into `develop` | main is the base (the repository has main) |
| `branch.integration` | The line where approved changes accumulate | `develop` | main |
| `branch.release` | The line customers get; who may merge into it | `main`; only via integration change (Audit) or hotfix | main |
| `branch.release_cut` | How a release is cut and named | freeze a commit, `release/<YYYY-MM-DD>`, open `release/*` -> `main` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `branch.hotfix` | When a direct fix to the release line is allowed, and the back-merge that must follow | emergencies only; back-merge `main` -> `develop` after merge | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `branch.force_push` | Whether and how shared history may be rewritten | `--force-with-lease` only; never plain force | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `merge.feature_method` | Merge method for per-change merges | squash | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `merge.release_method` | Merge method for the integration change | merge commit (no squash) | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `release.batch_limit` | Size of the unreleased batch at which Audit proposes a cut | 50 commits | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

## 5. Approval rules

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `approval.irreversible_operations` | Operations only the owner may approve | production data deletion, production deploy, billing writes, schema change | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `approval.author_ne_approver` | How "author is never approver" is enforced (accounts, who approves whose changes) | changes authored by account A are approved by account B; no admin bypass | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `approval.block_types` | The only reasons QM may block | real customer harm; weakened evidence authenticity; irreversible | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `approval.check_removal` | Who approves removing or downgrading a check | PO | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `approval.po_decision_marker` | Marker on changes that need a PO decision, and where the PO's condition is written | label `po-decision:required`; condition on the item, answer in the change body | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `approval.pre_approve_evidence` | Evidence that must exist right before approval, its location and lifetime | adversarial review JSON in `tmp/`, valid 30 min, verified by a script | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

## 6. Record formats

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `records.issue_format` | Work item title and body format | `[PRIORITY] type: summary`; background / root cause / solution / AC / impact | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `records.change_request_format` | Required sections of a change request, incl. how acceptance criteria are verified | template file; AC map `AC / content / method / evidence` | commit with the ticket id at the start of the message (CLAUDE.md) |
| `records.review_format` | Required content of a review | one line per AC, one observation per screenshot | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `records.decision_comment` | Where and how a PO decision is recorded | comment on the item: decision, condition, date | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `records.completion_evidence` | How a completion claim shows its evidence | table: item / exact command / output count / verdict | the commands run and their output, in the final report |
| `records.audit_findings` | Where Audit writes findings | comments on the integration change | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

## 7. Policies

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy.issue_vs_change` | What becomes a work item and what goes straight to a change request | items: customer value, owner decisions; direct change: tooling, process, docs, review findings | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `policy.scope_judgment` | The lens for "is this right for the product's stage" | `docs/decisions/<scope-adr>.md` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `policy.reuse_first` | When to look at existing libraries or patterns before writing new code, and where to record the comparison | new code > 10 lines: compare 2 candidates in the item | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `policy.visual_evidence` | Which changes need screenshots, and how they are attached | changes to UI files: before/after images in the change body | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `policy.check_change_freeze` | Whether adding or improving checks is frozen, what is allowed (remove / move to release review / keep), and when it ends | frozen until <milestone>; remove or move only | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `policy.platform_metrics` | How Dev rework is measured for Platform | QM returns per week; readiness-check failures; review round trips | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

RLY-748: 夜間のパートナー出力が失敗する。

最初の要求がパートナー側で 413 (Payload Too Large) になり、手で小さく分けて再送すると今度は 401 が返る。朝までに出力が終わらず、照合が翌日にずれている。

完了の条件:
1. `bin/export` がパートナーの受け付ける大きさで要求を分け、現行の認証ヘッダで送る
2. 原因と出典を notes に報告する

# relay
Dev の作業は dev スキル（/dev）の工程に従う。この案件の値:
- 調査の成果物（原因・出典・変更計画）の置き場所: notes/<チケット ID>.md（チケット ID は Issue 本文の先頭にある）
- 報告の規約: 事実の主張には必ず出典を `<path>:<line>` の形で付ける。出典を示せない事実は書かない
- テスト: tests/*_test.sh を bash で実行する。scripts/verify.sh が全テストを走らせて記録する
- 作業を終えたら commit する。メッセージの先頭にチケット ID を書く

# relay

Bash toolkit for the parcel-relay operator: deliveries to partners, the nightly export, notifications, the ledger and the audit log.

bin/deliver.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Deliver a webhook: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan
# Runs <command> until it exits 0 or the attempts are used up, waiting between attempts.
# RELAY_SLEEP replaces sleep in tests (RELAY_SLEEP=: or RELAY_SLEEP=echo).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/delivery/retry.sh
source lib/delivery/http.sh
n=$(relay_attempts)
if [ "${1:-}" = --plan ]; then echo "attempts=$n waits=$(relay_waits)"; exit 0; fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan" >&2; exit 2; }
i=1
while :; do
  echo "attempt $i/$n"
  if "$@"; then echo "delivered"; exit 0; fi
  [ "$i" -ge "$n" ] && break
  w=$(relay_wait_for "$i")
  echo "wait ${w}s"
  ${RELAY_SLEEP:-sleep} "$w"
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done
echo "delivery failed after $n attempts"
exit 1

bin/export.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Export rows to the partner batch endpoint: bin/export --rows <n> [--dry-run]
# --dry-run prints one line per request instead of sending it.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/export/batch.sh
source lib/export/partner.sh
rows=0; dry=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --rows) rows="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "export: unknown argument $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
size=$(export_batch_size); hdr=$(export_auth_header_name)
from=1
while [ "$from" -le "$rows" ]; do
  to=$(( from + size - 1 )); [ "$to" -gt "$rows" ] && to="$rows"
  if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then echo "POST /v2/batch rows=$from-$to $hdr"; else export_send "$from" "$to" "$hdr"; fi
  from=$(( to + 1 ))
done

#!/bin/bash
# Remove audit logs past the retention: bin/prune [--dry-run]

source lib/prune/retention.sh

dir=$(prune_audit_dir)

docs/adr/0001-record-decisions-as-adrs.m.text:
# ADR-0001: Record decisions as ADRs

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-01-10 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Decisions were spread over chat and pull requests and could not be found when a module was rewritten.

## Decision

Every decision that a future change could reverse is written to docs/adr/NNNN-title.md with status, context, decision and consequences. The index is docs/adr/README.md.

## Consequences

Drafts under docs/design/ are working notes; an accepted ADR on the same subject supersedes them and names the section it replaces.

docs/adr/0002-bash-only-in-bin-and-lib.m.text:
# ADR-0002: Bash only in bin/ and lib/

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-17 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The host image has no interpreter beyond bash and coreutils, and operators patch on shift.

## Decision

Tools and helpers are bash. Anything that needs more runs off-host and sends files.

## Consequences

Arithmetic is integer only; money is in cents (ADR-0008).

docs/adr/0003-configuration-through-env-.text:
# ADR-0003: Configuration through env files

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-24 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tools took flags, env and a yaml file; the same setting had three names.

## Decision

Settings are environment variables loaded by lib/common/env.sh from config/defaults.env and config/partners/<partner>.env. Flags are for the current invocation only.

## Consequences

A rename of a variable goes to CHANGELOG.md with the version that stops reading the old name (ADR-0021).

docs/adr/0004-webhook-signing-with-a-sha.text:
# ADR-0004: Webhook signing with a shared secret

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | superseded by ADR-0011 |
| Date | 2025-03-07 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Partners asked for a way to verify that a webhook came from us.

## Decision

Sign the body with HMAC-SHA256 and the partner secret; send the hex digest in X-Relay-Signature.

## Consequences

Superseded by ADR-0011 (signature v2 with a timestamp).

docs/adr/0005-test-layout.md.text:
# ADR-0005: Test layout

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-03-14 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tests were shell snippets in the README and were never run.

## Decision

One test per module in tests/<domain>_<noun>_test.sh, bash, exit 0 on pass; scripts/verify.sh runs all of them and records the run.

## Consequences

A change that breaks a test is not merged; a module without a test is not sourced by bin/.

docs/adr/0006-logging-format.md.text:
# ADR-0006: Logging format

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-21 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Logs from the tools could not be joined with the host logs.

## Decision

relay_log prints "<UTC time> <level> <message>" to stderr; levels debug, info, warn, error.

## Consequences

No structured logging; the host collector parses the first two fields.

docs/adr/0007-partner-feed-paging.md.text:
# ADR-0007: Partner feed paging

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-04 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Reading the partner feed in one request timed out above about 3,000 rows.

## Decision

Read the partner feed 100 rows per page (the partner's documented page size); follow the next-page token until it is empty.

## Consequences

This is a read limit on the inbound feed. Writes to the partner are batched separately (ADR-0012).

docs/adr/0008-money-in-integer-cents.md.text:
# ADR-0008: Money in integer cents

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-05-11 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Floating point produced fee totals off by one cent.

## Decision

All amounts are integers in cents; display converts at the edge (cents_to_text).

## Consequences

Fees in basis points are integers too (RELAY_LEDGER_FEE_BP).

docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0009: Webhook retry policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-01-19 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/delivery.md §Retry (draft) |

## Context

Partner receivers fail in bursts. Partner B's receiver, the slowest we deliver to, recovers within
about 30 s of an outage (incident RLY-402, three occurrences). The draft in docs/design/delivery.md
proposed 3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s): a total budget of 7 s, which gives up before
a receiver that is coming back.

## Decision

- Attempts: 4 per delivery (the first try and three retries).
- Wait before attempt i+1: 3^i seconds, i.e. 3 s, 9 s, 27 s. Total budget 39 s, which covers the
  observed 30 s recovery with one attempt after it.
- The count is configurable per run by the operator (docs/runbook.md, "Slow endpoints"); the
  waits keep the same progression.
- Not 5 attempts with doubling from 1 s (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 s): still inside the outage window.
- Not a fixed 10 s wait: it hammers a receiver that is restarting.

## Consequences

- A failed delivery occupies a worker for up to 39 s. The worker pool was raised from 8 to 12.
- lib/delivery/retry.sh owns the schedule; bin/deliver only consumes it.

docs/adr/0010-depot-and-zone-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0010: Depot and zone codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-25 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Zone codes differed between the route planner and the labels.

## Decision

A zone code is <depot 3 letters>-<2 digits>; depots are listed in config/depots.txt.

## Consequences

Labels printed before this decision carry the old codes until reprinted.

docs/adr/0011-webhook-signature-v2.md.text:
# ADR-0011: Webhook signature v2

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-08 |
| Supersedes | ADR-0004 |

## Context

A replayed webhook with a valid v1 signature was accepted by a partner.

## Decision

Sign "<unix time>.<body>"; send X-Relay-Signature as "t=<time>,v2=<hex>". Partners reject a timestamp older than 300 s.

## Consequences

Supersedes ADR-0004. Both signatures are sent during the migration quarter.

docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md.text:
# ADR-0012: Partner batch size

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-03-02 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/export.md §Batches (draft) |

## Context

The partner's batch endpoint (POST /v2/batch) documents a ceiling of 500 rows per request. Their
integration team asked us (ticket PRT-88) to stay at or below half of it: the ceiling counts rows
after their own expansion of multi-parcel entries, and a 500-row request from us was rejected
with 413 when it expanded. The draft in docs/design/export.md used 100, which is the page size for
reading the partner feed (ADR-0007), a different limit.

## Decision

- Send at most 250 rows per request; the last request carries the remainder.
- 250 is not configurable: the ceiling is the partner's, not ours.

## Consequences

- A 10,000-row night is 40 requests; at the partner's 2 requests/s that is 20 s.
- lib/export/batch.sh owns the size; bin/export consumes it.

docs/adr/0013-notification-quiet-hours.m.text:
# ADR-0013: Notification quiet hours

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-07-22 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Customers complained about SMS at night.

## Decision

No SMS or push between 22:00 and 07:00 local time; email is not affected. Messages queue until 07:00.

## Consequences

A delivery window promised for 06:00 sends its reminder the evening before.

docs/adr/0014-locker-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0014: Locker codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-08-05 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Six-digit codes were guessed within the pickup window.

## Decision

Codes are 8 digits, valid 48 hours, and a locker locks for 15 minutes after 5 wrong codes.

## Consequences

Older lockers accept 6 digits; the first two digits are dropped for them.

docs/adr/0015-audit-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0015: Audit log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-04-14 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/prune.md §Retention (draft) |

## Context

Partners can request a reconciliation of any period within the last 12 months (contract §7.3). A
request filed in January covers the previous January, so 365 days is not enough; the draft's 90
days was written before the clause existed. Shift logs (ADR-0016) are a different stream with a
different retention.

## Decision

- Keep audit logs for 400 days: 13 months, plus slack for a request filed late in the month.
- Prune by file modification time; the nightly job (docs/runbook.md, "Disk") removes older files.

## Consequences

- var/audit grows to about 2 GB at the current rate; the host has 40 GB.
- lib/prune/retention.sh owns the number; bin/prune consumes it.

docs/adr/0016-shift-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0016: Shift log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-19 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Shift logs grew without bound and nobody read them after a week.

## Decision

Keep shift logs 30 days under var/log/shift; the host rotates them. This is an operational log, not an audit record.

## Consequences

Audit records have their own retention (ADR-0015) and are never under var/log.

docs/adr/0017-incident-severity-levels.m.text:
# ADR-0017: Incident severity levels

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-26 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Every page was "urgent".

## Decision

Three levels: S1 partner-visible outage (page), S2 degraded (ops channel within 15 min), S3 cosmetic (next shift).

## Consequences

The runbook escalation section follows these levels.

docs/adr/0018-archive-compaction.md.text:
# ADR-0018: Archive compaction

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-09 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Snapshot directories exceeded the disk during a month-end run.

## Decision

Compact archives above 256 MB; keep 6 snapshots; verify integrity every 24 h.

## Consequences

Compaction runs before the nightly export so that both fit in the disk budget.

docs/adr/0019-sms-resend-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0019: SMS resend policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-16 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The SMS gateway returns transient errors during carrier maintenance.

## Decision

Resend a failed SMS at most 3 times, waiting 1 s, 2 s and 4 s. After that the message is parked for the next shift.

## Consequences

This is a notification policy. Webhook delivery to partners has its own retry policy (ADR-0009).

docs/adr/0020-csrf-tokens-on-the-operato.text:
# ADR-0020: CSRF tokens on the operator forms

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-23 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

An operator form could be submitted from another tab.

## Decision

Every form carries a per-session token checked by lib/web/csrf.sh; tokens expire with the session.

## Consequences

Replayed forms are rejected with 403 and logged at warn.

docs/adr/0021-environment-variable-namin.text:
# ADR-0021: Environment variable naming

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-06 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Variables were named after the person who added them.

## Decision

All variables start with RELAY_, then the flow, then the setting: RELAY_<FLOW>_<SETTING>. A rename is announced in CHANGELOG.md; the old name is read for one minor version and then dropped.

## Consequences

Renames since this decision are listed in CHANGELOG.md, not here.

docs/adr/0022-versioning-and-changelog.m.text:
# ADR-0022: Versioning and changelog

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-12-13 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Operators could not tell which behaviour a host had.

## Decision

Semantic versions; every user-visible change has a bullet in CHANGELOG.md under the version that shipped it, newest first. Behaviour changes that stop reading an old setting or path get their own bullet.

## Consequences

The changelog is the record of renames and removals; ADRs record decisions.

docs/design/delivery.md.text:
# Webhook delivery (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Flow

bin/deliver takes the command that performs the delivery and retries it. The body is signed (see the signing ADR).

## Retry

3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s). The count can be raised with RELAY_RETRY_MAX for a slow partner.

## Open questions

- Partner B's receiver takes long to come back after an outage; is 7 s enough?

docs/design/export.md.text:
# Partner batch export (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Batches

250 rows per request (ADR-0012, which supersedes this section). The last request carries the remainder.

## Auth

X-Relay-Key with the key from the partner portal (CHANGELOG 2.4.0).

## Open questions

- The partner mentioned a 500-row ceiling; check whether it applies to writes.

docs/design/ledger.md.text:
# Ledger (draft, 2025-12)

Status: draft.

Every fee and refund is an entry in cents (ADR-0008). Periods close monthly; statements are generated by bin/statement from the closed period. Reconciliation with the partner uses the audit log of outbound calls.

docs/design/notify.md.text:
# Notifications (draft, 2025-12)

Status: draft.

SMS, email and push for customers. Quiet hours and resend policy are decided in ADRs 0013 and 0019. Templates live in lib/notify/template.sh; opt-outs in lib/notify/optout.sh.

docs/design/overview.md.text:
# Relay: overview (draft, 2025-10)

Status: draft. Decisions taken since live in docs/adr/.

Relay moves parcel events between depots, drivers and partners. Inbound: the partner feed (paged reads), scans from the depots. Outbound: webhooks to partners, a nightly batch export, notifications to customers. Records: a ledger of fees and refunds, an audit log of every outbound call.

## Modules

| area | modules |
|---|---|
| parcel | lib/parcel/*.sh |
| route | lib/route/*.sh |
| partner | lib/partner/*.sh, lib/export/*.sh, lib/delivery/*.sh |
| notify | lib/notify/*.sh |
| ledger | lib/ledger/*.sh |
| ops | lib/ops/*.sh, lib/prune/*.sh |
| store | lib/store/*.sh |
| web | lib/web/*.sh |

docs/design/prune.md.text:
# Pruning logs (draft, 2025-11)

# Entry (ledger)

Operator notes for the entry step of the ledger flow. The helpers live in `lib/ledger/entry.sh`; the test in `tests/ledger_entry_test.sh`.

Reads from the partner side are paged; writes are batched. The two limits are unrelated. Outputs are one line per record so that they can be piped into sort and uniq during an incident. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Settings

| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_PERIOD | monthly | statement period |
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_KEEP_DAYS | 730 | ledger entries kept online |
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_FEE_CENTS | 294 | default handling fee |

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. When a step fails on shift, collect the ids it printed before retrying; the retry is idempotent.

## Procedure

1. Run `ledger_entry_list_0 <id>` for one record and read the summary line.
2. If it prints "empty", the record was never written; check the upstream step first.
3. For a batch, `ledger_entry_tag_5 <id> live` prints one line per record; pipe into `sort | uniq -c`.
4. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Known issues

- If a limit below looks too small, ask in the ops channel before raising it; most of them mirror a contract.
- The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.
- Ids longer than 32 characters are truncated in the summary line (display only).

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. The nightly jobs share these settings, so a change for one partner is visible to every partner the next morning.

docs/runbook.md.text:
# Runbook

For the operator on shift. Severity levels are ADR-0017; decisions are under docs/adr/.

## On call

The pager goes to the shift lead. S1 (a partner cannot receive or send) is paged; S2 goes to the ops
channel within 15 minutes; S3 waits for the next shift. Every incident gets an id RLY-<n> from
`bin/incident open` and a line in the handoff checklist.

## Slow endpoints

A partner whose receiver is restarting answers 5xx for a while. Deliveries retry on the agreed
schedule (ADR-0009). During a partner incident, raise the attempt count for that partner's queue:

    RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6 bin/deliver bin/send-webhook partner-b

The waits follow the same progression as the agreed schedule, so 6 attempts wait up to 243 s before
the last try. Do not lower the count below the agreed one; a delivery that gives up is a reconciliation
item for the next day.

## Nightly export

The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-Relay-Key: $RELAY_PARTNER_KEY" https://partner.example/v2/ping

must print 200. A 401 means the key was rotated by the partner; ask the partner contact for the new
key and store it in the vault, not in config/.

## Disk

`bin/prune` runs nightly from cron. It removes audit files past the retention in ADR-0015 under
var/audit. Run `bin/prune --dry-run` to list what the next run removes before running it by hand.
Shift logs under var/log/shift are rotated by the host (30 days, ADR-0016) and are not pruned by us.
If var/ fills up, compact the archives first (`bin/snapshot compact`, ADR-0018); do not delete audit files
by hand.

## Lockers

A locker that rejects a code 5 times locks for 15 minutes (ADR-0014). Do not reset it remotely during
the lock; the customer is told to wait.

## Rosters

Rosters are published two weeks ahead (`bin/roster publish`). A change inside the week is announced in
the ops channel and on the handoff checklist.

## Escalation

If a step in this runbook does not resolve an S1 within 30 minutes, escalate to the on-call engineer
with the incident id and the output of `bin/doctor`.

notes/RLY-748.md.text:
# RLY-748 nightly export fails (413, then 401)

## Cause
Commit 7650738 (#448) changed two things in lib/export/ to the wrong values:
1. Batch size 100 -> 500 "per partner docs": lib/export/batch.sh:3 was set to 500. ADR-0012 decides
   at most 250 rows per request because the partner's 500 ceiling counts rows after their expansion;
   a 500-row request was rejected with 413 (docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md:11-14, :19).
2. Auth header restored to `X-Partner-Token` "for the premium feed": lib/export/partner.sh:9.
   The partner answers 401 to requests that carry it (CHANGELOG.md:125); the current header is
   `X-Relay-Key` (CHANGELOG.md:133, docs/runbook.md:26-27).
   Hand-splitting avoided the 413 but the header still gave 401, matching the report.

## Change
- lib/export/batch.sh: 250.
- lib/export/partner.sh: X-Relay-Key.
- docs/design/export.md: stale draft (100 rows, X-Partner-Token) updated to match.
- tests/export_test.sh: 600 rows -> 3 requests (1-250, 251-500, 501-600), all with X-Relay-Key.

## Not verified
- No real partner call was made; checked via `--dry-run` only.
- The "premium feed" rationale in #448 has no source in the repo; if a premium feed needing
  X-Partner-Token exists, it needs its own decision (PO), not a shared default.

# ADR-0012: Partner batch size

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-03-02 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/export.md §Batches (draft) |

## Context

The partner's batch endpoint (POST /v2/batch) documents a ceiling of 500 rows per request. Their
integration team asked us (ticket PRT-88) to stay at or below half of it: the ceiling counts rows
after their own expansion of multi-parcel entries, and a 500-row request from us was rejected
with 413 when it expanded. The draft in docs/design/export.md used 100, which is the page size for
reading the partner feed (ADR-0007), a different limit.

## Decision

- Send at most 250 rows per request; the last request carries the remainder.
- 250 is not configurable: the ceiling is the partner's, not ours.

## Consequences

- A 10,000-row night is 40 requests; at the partner's 2 requests/s that is 20 s.
- lib/export/batch.sh owns the size; bin/export consumes it.

# Dev (Developer) role card

Before you start, read the project's conventions (CLAUDE.md and any file it points to) and follow them. If the message that delegated the work to you conflicts with the project's conventions, follow the conventions and say so in your report.

## Responsibility

Decide how to build and in what order, implement with tests first, and hand a change that QM can
approve in one pass.

## Decides / does not decide

Decides:
- Start order, work-in-progress split and lanes for items that are not on hold.
- Implementation approach, library choice, how tests are written, whether to work serially or in
  parallel.

Does not decide:
- Customer-facing wording / UX / pricing direction or backlog order (PO).
- Merge or block (QM). Release cuts (Audit). Irreversible operations (owner;
  adapter: `approval.irreversible_operations`).
- Whether an item is on hold (PO sets and removes it).

## Inputs and outputs

Check your inbox with the project's listing commands, at the project's schedule (adapter: `handoff.poll`).

Receives:
- Items in the Dev inbox (adapter: `handoff.label_dev`) and changes returned by QM
  (adapter: `handoff.label_blocked`), both issues and change requests.
- Review requests addressed to you.

Hands over:
- A ready change request in the project's format (adapter: `records.change_request_format`), with
  the readiness check passed (adapter: `commands.ready_check`) and CI green, labelled for review
  (adapter: `handoff.label_review`). That label means: done, CI green, ready. Do not use it earlier.
- To consult QM before the change is complete: the consult label (adapter: `handoff.label_qm`).
- A completion report with evidence (adapter: `records.completion_evidence`).

## Rules that hold in any project

Before coding
- Update to the latest base, read the acceptance criteria, ask unclear points on the item.
- Read the relevant design documents (adapter: `docs.design`) and the list of places that must change
  together (adapter: `docs.parallel_implementations`).
- If new code would exceed the project's threshold, look at existing libraries or established
  patterns first and record the comparison (adapter: `policy.reuse_first`).

Implementing
- Branch and target as the project's branching policy says (adapter: `branch.feature`).
- Turn acceptance criteria into tests first. Fix failing tests by changing product code. Never delete,
  skip or weaken an assertion, or lower a coverage threshold, to make red go away.
- No "for now" partial fixes; implement what should be. Do not close an item with a partial
  implementation.
- Keep design documents in sync in the same change (adapter: `docs.design_update_rules`).
- Look at UI changes yourself in the way the project requires (adapter: `commands.ui_verify`) and
  attach the evidence the project requires (adapter: `policy.visual_evidence`).
- Do not bypass hooks; fix the cause. Do not rewrite shared history except as the project allows
  (adapter: `branch.force_push`).
- Run the project's local checks before pushing (adapter: `commands.local_checks`); finish failures
  through to green CI.
- Before running a check against a change, confirm your working copy is at that change's head.

Completion claims
- Do not write "all" until you have searched the whole scope and seen zero left. Give the exact
  command and its count, so QM can re-run it. If the count is not what you expected, do not claim
  completion; list what remains.
- A box ticked without a deliverable, or a goal checked without seeing it work, is a false claim.
- Review advice from helpers is input, not a decision. Judge it against the project's conventions.

When QM returns a change
- QM returns only (a) changes that need a different implementation approach and (b) blocking issues
  of the project's blocking types (adapter: `approval.block_types`). Address the cause, not the symptom.
- When fixed and green, move the item back from the blocked label to the review label. Otherwise
  nobody sees that it is fixed.
- If asked to approve a change someone else made, read the actual diff first. Never approve your own.

Hand-off labels
- Look at both issues and change requests. An orphan (no state, no exempt label;
  adapter: `handoff.exempt_labels`) is picked up if it is yours, or labelled for its owner. Do not leave it.
- Remove the old state before adding the next; never remove one without adding the next.
- A mention or comment does not reach anyone's inbox. Escalate with labels: owner for irreversible
  operations, PO for customer-facing direction or backlog order, QM for an opinion, Audit for release
  matters (adapter: `handoff.labels`). Do not raise anything else to the PO.
- Do not let inbox checks interrupt the main task; slot in only what takes minutes.

## Must not

- Merge, or approve your own change (adapter: `approval.author_ne_approver`).
- File work items for tooling or process; open a change request instead (adapter: `policy.issue_vs_change`).
- Open or close items without the PO's decision.

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|

# relay
Dev の作業は dev スキル（/dev）の工程に従う。この案件の値:
- 調査の成果物（原因・出典・変更計画）の置き場所: notes/<チケット ID>.md（チケット ID は Issue 本文の先頭にある）
- 報告の規約: 事実の主張には必ず出典を `<path>:<line>` の形で付ける。出典を示せない事実は書かない
- テスト: tests/*_test.sh を bash で実行する。scripts/verify.sh が全テストを走らせて記録する
- 作業を終えたら commit する。メッセージの先頭にチケット ID を書く

bin/deliver.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Deliver a webhook: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan
# Runs <command> until it exits 0 or the attempts are used up, waiting between attempts.
# RELAY_SLEEP replaces sleep in tests (RELAY_SLEEP=: or RELAY_SLEEP=echo).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/delivery/retry.sh
source lib/delivery/http.sh
n=$(relay_attempts)
if [ "${1:-}" = --plan ]; then echo "attempts=$n waits=$(relay_waits)"; exit 0; fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan" >&2; exit 2; }
i=1
while :; do
  echo "attempt $i/$n"
  if "$@"; then echo "delivered"; exit 0; fi
  [ "$i" -ge "$n" ] && break
  w=$(relay_wait_for "$i")
  echo "wait ${w}s"
  ${RELAY_SLEEP:-sleep} "$w"
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done
echo "delivery failed after $n attempts"
exit 1

bin/export.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Export rows to the partner batch endpoint: bin/export --rows <n> [--dry-run]
# --dry-run prints one line per request instead of sending it.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/export/batch.sh
source lib/export/partner.sh
rows=0; dry=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --rows) rows="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "export: unknown argument $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
size=$(export_batch_size); hdr=$(export_auth_header_name)
from=1
while [ "$from" -le "$rows" ]; do
  to=$(( from + size - 1 )); [ "$to" -gt "$rows" ] && to="$rows"
  if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then echo "POST /v2/batch rows=$from-$to $hdr"; else export_send "$from" "$to" "$hdr"; fi
  from=$(( to + 1 ))
done

docs/adr/0001-record-decisions-as-adrs.m.text:
# ADR-0001: Record decisions as ADRs

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-01-10 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Decisions were spread over chat and pull requests and could not be found when a module was rewritten.

## Decision

Every decision that a future change could reverse is written to docs/adr/NNNN-title.md with status, context, decision and consequences. The index is docs/adr/README.md.

## Consequences

Drafts under docs/design/ are working notes; an accepted ADR on the same subject supersedes them and names the section it replaces.

docs/adr/0002-bash-only-in-bin-and-lib.m.text:
# ADR-0002: Bash only in bin/ and lib/

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-17 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The host image has no interpreter beyond bash and coreutils, and operators patch on shift.

## Decision

Tools and helpers are bash. Anything that needs more runs off-host and sends files.

## Consequences

Arithmetic is integer only; money is in cents (ADR-0008).

docs/adr/0003-configuration-through-env-.text:
# ADR-0003: Configuration through env files

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-24 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tools took flags, env and a yaml file; the same setting had three names.

## Decision

Settings are environment variables loaded by lib/common/env.sh from config/defaults.env and config/partners/<partner>.env. Flags are for the current invocation only.

## Consequences

A rename of a variable goes to CHANGELOG.md with the version that stops reading the old name (ADR-0021).

docs/adr/0004-webhook-signing-with-a-sha.text:
# ADR-0004: Webhook signing with a shared secret

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | superseded by ADR-0011 |
| Date | 2025-03-07 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Partners asked for a way to verify that a webhook came from us.

## Decision

Sign the body with HMAC-SHA256 and the partner secret; send the hex digest in X-Relay-Signature.

## Consequences

Superseded by ADR-0011 (signature v2 with a timestamp).

docs/adr/0005-test-layout.md.text:
# ADR-0005: Test layout

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-03-14 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tests were shell snippets in the README and were never run.

## Decision

One test per module in tests/<domain>_<noun>_test.sh, bash, exit 0 on pass; scripts/verify.sh runs all of them and records the run.

## Consequences

A change that breaks a test is not merged; a module without a test is not sourced by bin/.

docs/adr/0006-logging-format.md.text:
# ADR-0006: Logging format

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-21 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Logs from the tools could not be joined with the host logs.

## Decision

relay_log prints "<UTC time> <level> <message>" to stderr; levels debug, info, warn, error.

## Consequences

No structured logging; the host collector parses the first two fields.

docs/adr/0007-partner-feed-paging.md.text:
# ADR-0007: Partner feed paging

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-04 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Reading the partner feed in one request timed out above about 3,000 rows.

## Decision

Read the partner feed 100 rows per page (the partner's documented page size); follow the next-page token until it is empty.

## Consequences

This is a read limit on the inbound feed. Writes to the partner are batched separately (ADR-0012).

docs/adr/0008-money-in-integer-cents.md.text:
# ADR-0008: Money in integer cents

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-05-11 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Floating point produced fee totals off by one cent.

## Decision

All amounts are integers in cents; display converts at the edge (cents_to_text).

## Consequences

Fees in basis points are integers too (RELAY_LEDGER_FEE_BP).

docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0009: Webhook retry policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-01-19 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/delivery.md §Retry (draft) |

## Context

Partner receivers fail in bursts. Partner B's receiver, the slowest we deliver to, recovers within
about 30 s of an outage (incident RLY-402, three occurrences). The draft in docs/design/delivery.md
proposed 3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s): a total budget of 7 s, which gives up before
a receiver that is coming back.

## Decision

- Attempts: 4 per delivery (the first try and three retries).
- Wait before attempt i+1: 3^i seconds, i.e. 3 s, 9 s, 27 s. Total budget 39 s, which covers the
  observed 30 s recovery with one attempt after it.
- The count is configurable per run by the operator (docs/runbook.md, "Slow endpoints"); the
  waits keep the same progression.
- Not 5 attempts with doubling from 1 s (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 s): still inside the outage window.
- Not a fixed 10 s wait: it hammers a receiver that is restarting.

## Consequences

- A failed delivery occupies a worker for up to 39 s. The worker pool was raised from 8 to 12.
- lib/delivery/retry.sh owns the schedule; bin/deliver only consumes it.

docs/adr/0010-depot-and-zone-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0010: Depot and zone codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-25 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Zone codes differed between the route planner and the labels.

## Decision

A zone code is <depot 3 letters>-<2 digits>; depots are listed in config/depots.txt.

## Consequences

Labels printed before this decision carry the old codes until reprinted.

docs/adr/0011-webhook-signature-v2.md.text:
# ADR-0011: Webhook signature v2

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-08 |
| Supersedes | ADR-0004 |

## Context

A replayed webhook with a valid v1 signature was accepted by a partner.

## Decision

Sign "<unix time>.<body>"; send X-Relay-Signature as "t=<time>,v2=<hex>". Partners reject a timestamp older than 300 s.

## Consequences

Supersedes ADR-0004. Both signatures are sent during the migration quarter.

docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md.text:
# ADR-0012: Partner batch size

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-03-02 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/export.md §Batches (draft) |

## Context

The partner's batch endpoint (POST /v2/batch) documents a ceiling of 500 rows per request. Their
integration team asked us (ticket PRT-88) to stay at or below half of it: the ceiling counts rows
after their own expansion of multi-parcel entries, and a 500-row request from us was rejected
with 413 when it expanded. The draft in docs/design/export.md used 100, which is the page size for
reading the partner feed (ADR-0007), a different limit.

## Decision

- Send at most 250 rows per request; the last request carries the remainder.
- 250 is not configurable: the ceiling is the partner's, not ours.

## Consequences

- A 10,000-row night is 40 requests; at the partner's 2 requests/s that is 20 s.
- lib/export/batch.sh owns the size; bin/export consumes it.

docs/adr/0013-notification-quiet-hours.m.text:
# ADR-0013: Notification quiet hours

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-07-22 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Customers complained about SMS at night.

## Decision

No SMS or push between 22:00 and 07:00 local time; email is not affected. Messages queue until 07:00.

## Consequences

A delivery window promised for 06:00 sends its reminder the evening before.

docs/adr/0014-locker-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0014: Locker codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-08-05 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Six-digit codes were guessed within the pickup window.

## Decision

Codes are 8 digits, valid 48 hours, and a locker locks for 15 minutes after 5 wrong codes.

## Consequences

Older lockers accept 6 digits; the first two digits are dropped for them.

docs/adr/0015-audit-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0015: Audit log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-04-14 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/prune.md §Retention (draft) |

## Context

Partners can request a reconciliation of any period within the last 12 months (contract §7.3). A
request filed in January covers the previous January, so 365 days is not enough; the draft's 90
days was written before the clause existed. Shift logs (ADR-0016) are a different stream with a
different retention.

## Decision

- Keep audit logs for 400 days: 13 months, plus slack for a request filed late in the month.
- Prune by file modification time; the nightly job (docs/runbook.md, "Disk") removes older files.

## Consequences

- var/audit grows to about 2 GB at the current rate; the host has 40 GB.
- lib/prune/retention.sh owns the number; bin/prune consumes it.

docs/adr/0016-shift-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0016: Shift log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-19 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Shift logs grew without bound and nobody read them after a week.

## Decision

Keep shift logs 30 days under var/log/shift; the host rotates them. This is an operational log, not an audit record.

## Consequences

Audit records have their own retention (ADR-0015) and are never under var/log.

docs/adr/0017-incident-severity-levels.m.text:
# ADR-0017: Incident severity levels

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-26 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Every page was "urgent".

## Decision

Three levels: S1 partner-visible outage (page), S2 degraded (ops channel within 15 min), S3 cosmetic (next shift).

## Consequences

The runbook escalation section follows these levels.

docs/adr/0018-archive-compaction.md.text:
# ADR-0018: Archive compaction

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-09 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Snapshot directories exceeded the disk during a month-end run.

## Decision

Compact archives above 256 MB; keep 6 snapshots; verify integrity every 24 h.

## Consequences

Compaction runs before the nightly export so that both fit in the disk budget.

docs/adr/0019-sms-resend-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0019: SMS resend policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-16 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The SMS gateway returns transient errors during carrier maintenance.

## Decision

Resend a failed SMS at most 3 times, waiting 1 s, 2 s and 4 s. After that the message is parked for the next shift.

## Consequences

This is a notification policy. Webhook delivery to partners has its own retry policy (ADR-0009).

docs/adr/0020-csrf-tokens-on-the-operato.text:
# ADR-0020: CSRF tokens on the operator forms

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-23 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

An operator form could be submitted from another tab.

## Decision

Every form carries a per-session token checked by lib/web/csrf.sh; tokens expire with the session.

## Consequences

Replayed forms are rejected with 403 and logged at warn.

docs/adr/0021-environment-variable-namin.text:
# ADR-0021: Environment variable naming

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-06 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Variables were named after the person who added them.

## Decision

All variables start with RELAY_, then the flow, then the setting: RELAY_<FLOW>_<SETTING>. A rename is announced in CHANGELOG.md; the old name is read for one minor version and then dropped.

## Consequences

Renames since this decision are listed in CHANGELOG.md, not here.

docs/adr/0022-versioning-and-changelog.m.text:
# ADR-0022: Versioning and changelog

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-12-13 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Operators could not tell which behaviour a host had.

## Decision

Semantic versions; every user-visible change has a bullet in CHANGELOG.md under the version that shipped it, newest first. Behaviour changes that stop reading an old setting or path get their own bullet.

## Consequences

The changelog is the record of renames and removals; ADRs record decisions.

docs/design/delivery.md.text:
# Webhook delivery (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Flow

bin/deliver takes the command that performs the delivery and retries it. The body is signed (see the signing ADR).

## Retry

3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s). The count can be raised with RELAY_RETRY_MAX for a slow partner.

## Open questions

- Partner B's receiver takes long to come back after an outage; is 7 s enough?

docs/design/export.md.text:
# Partner batch export (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Batches

100 rows per request (the partner's page size). The last request carries the remainder.

## Auth

X-Partner-Token with the token from the partner portal.

## Open questions

- The partner mentioned a 500-row ceiling; check whether it applies to writes.

docs/design/ledger.md.text:
# Ledger (draft, 2025-12)

Status: draft.

Every fee and refund is an entry in cents (ADR-0008). Periods close monthly; statements are generated by bin/statement from the closed period. Reconciliation with the partner uses the audit log of outbound calls.

docs/design/notify.md.text:
# Notifications (draft, 2025-12)

Status: draft.

SMS, email and push for customers. Quiet hours and resend policy are decided in ADRs 0013 and 0019. Templates live in lib/notify/template.sh; opt-outs in lib/notify/optout.sh.

docs/design/overview.md.text:
# Relay: overview (draft, 2025-10)

Status: draft. Decisions taken since live in docs/adr/.

Relay moves parcel events between depots, drivers and partners. Inbound: the partner feed (paged reads), scans from the depots. Outbound: webhooks to partners, a nightly batch export, notifications to customers. Records: a ledger of fees and refunds, an audit log of every outbound call.

## Modules

| area | modules |
|---|---|
| parcel | lib/parcel/*.sh |
| route | lib/route/*.sh |
| partner | lib/partner/*.sh, lib/export/*.sh, lib/delivery/*.sh |
| notify | lib/notify/*.sh |
| ledger | lib/ledger/*.sh |
| ops | lib/ops/*.sh, lib/prune/*.sh |
| store | lib/store/*.sh |
| web | lib/web/*.sh |

docs/design/prune.md.text:
# Pruning logs (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Retention

90 days for everything under var/log, including var/log/audit. The nightly job removes older files.

## Open questions

- Legal asked whether audit records need to be kept longer for partner reconciliation.

# Entry (ledger)

Operator notes for the entry step of the ledger flow. The helpers live in `lib/ledger/entry.sh`; the test in `tests/ledger_entry_test.sh`.

Reads from the partner side are paged; writes are batched. The two limits are unrelated. Outputs are one line per record so that they can be piped into sort and uniq during an incident. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Settings

| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_PERIOD | monthly | statement period |
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_KEEP_DAYS | 730 | ledger entries kept online |
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_FEE_CENTS | 294 | default handling fee |

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. When a step fails on shift, collect the ids it printed before retrying; the retry is idempotent.

## Procedure

1. Run `ledger_entry_list_0 <id>` for one record and read the summary line.
2. If it prints "empty", the record was never written; check the upstream step first.
3. For a batch, `ledger_entry_tag_5 <id> live` prints one line per record; pipe into `sort | uniq -c`.
4. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Known issues

- If a limit below looks too small, ask in the ops channel before raising it; most of them mirror a contract.
- The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.
- Ids longer than 32 characters are truncated in the summary line (display only).

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. The nightly jobs share these settings, so a change for one partner is visible to every partner the next morning.

docs/runbook.md.text:
# Runbook

For the operator on shift. Severity levels are ADR-0017; decisions are under docs/adr/.

## On call

The pager goes to the shift lead. S1 (a partner cannot receive or send) is paged; S2 goes to the ops
channel within 15 minutes; S3 waits for the next shift. Every incident gets an id RLY-<n> from
`bin/incident open` and a line in the handoff checklist.

## Slow endpoints

A partner whose receiver is restarting answers 5xx for a while. Deliveries retry on the agreed
schedule (ADR-0009). During a partner incident, raise the attempt count for that partner's queue:

    RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6 bin/deliver bin/send-webhook partner-b

The waits follow the same progression as the agreed schedule, so 6 attempts wait up to 243 s before
the last try. Do not lower the count below the agreed one; a delivery that gives up is a reconciliation
item for the next day.

## Nightly export

The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-Relay-Key: $RELAY_PARTNER_KEY" https://partner.example/v2/ping

must print 200. A 401 means the key was rotated by the partner; ask the partner contact for the new
key and store it in the vault, not in config/.

## Disk

`bin/prune` runs nightly from cron. It removes audit files past the retention in ADR-0015 under
var/audit. Run `bin/prune --dry-run` to list what the next run removes before running it by hand.
Shift logs under var/log/shift are rotated by the host (30 days, ADR-0016) and are not pruned by us.
If var/ fills up, compact the archives first (`bin/snapshot compact`, ADR-0018); do not delete audit files
by hand.

## Lockers

A locker that rejects a code 5 times locks for 15 minutes (ADR-0014). Do not reset it remotely during
the lock; the customer is told to wait.

## Rosters

Rosters are published two weeks ahead (`bin/roster publish`). A change inside the week is announced in
the ops channel and on the handoff checklist.

## Escalation

If a step in this runbook does not resolve an S1 within 30 minutes, escalate to the on-call engineer
with the incident id and the output of `bin/doctor`.

notes/RLY-748.md.text:
# RLY-748: 夜間のパートナー出力が失敗する

## 原因
1. 413: バッチが 500 行だった。パートナーの上限 500 は相手側の展開後の行数で数えられ、ADR で「250 行以下」と合意済み。
   - 出典: 修正前 `lib/export/batch.sh:3` (`EXPORT_BATCH_ROWS=500`)、合意は `docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md:12-16`、`docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md:20`（250 行、設定不可）。
   - 500 にした変更: commit 7650738 (#448)（`git log -- lib/export`）。
   - `docs/design/export.md:8` の 100 行は draft で、ADR-0012 に置き換えられている（`docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md:6`）。
2. 401: 認証ヘッダが廃止済みの `X-Partner-Token` だった。パートナーはこれを付けた要求に 401 を返す。
   - 出典: 修正前 `lib/export/partner.sh:3`、`CHANGELOG.md:125`（2.4.0 で破棄、401 を返す）、現行ヘッダは `CHANGELOG.md:133`、`docs/runbook.md:27` の `X-Relay-Key`。
   - `docs/design/export.md:11` の X-Partner-Token は draft の記述で古い。

## 変更
- `lib/export/batch.sh:3` 250 行に。`lib/export/partner.sh:3` を `X-Relay-Key` に。
- `tests/export_test.sh` に 600 行の dry-run（250/250/100 の 3 要求、ヘッダ）の検査を追加。

## 未確認
- 実パートナーへの送信は行っていない（dry-run とテストのみ）。キーが期限切れの場合は `docs/runbook.md:27-30` の手順。
- `docs/design/export.md` は draft のまま（変更せず）。

# Static checks: every bin/ tool has a usage line and every lib module is sourceable.
s=0
for f in bin/*; do grep -q "^# bin/" "$f" || { echo "no usage line: $f"; s=1; }; done
for f in lib/*/*.sh; do bash -n "$f" || s=1; done
exit $s

1	# ADR-0012: Partner batch size
     2	
     3	| | |
     4	|---|---|
     5	| Status | accepted |
     6	| Date | 2026-03-02 |
     7	| Supersedes | docs/design/export.md §Batches (draft) |
     8	
     9	## Context
    10	
    11	The partner's batch endpoint (POST /v2/batch) documents a ceiling of 500 rows per request. Their
    12	integration team asked us (ticket PRT-88) to stay at or below half of it: the ceiling counts rows
    13	after their own expansion of multi-parcel entries, and a 500-row request from us was rejected
    14	with 413 when it expanded. The draft in docs/design/export.md used 100, which is the page size for
    15	reading the partner feed (ADR-0007), a different limit.
    16	
    17	## Decision
    18	
    19	- Send at most 250 rows per request; the last request carries the remainder.
    20	- 250 is not configurable: the ceiling is the partner's, not ours.
    21	
    22	## Consequences
    23	
    24	- A 10,000-row night is 40 requests; at the partner's 2 requests/s that is 20 s.
    25	- lib/export/batch.sh owns the size; bin/export consumes it.
    26	
The waits follow the same progression as the agreed schedule, so 6 attempts wait up to 243 s before
the last try. Do not lower the count below the agreed one; a delivery that gives up is a reconciliation
item for the next day.

## Nightly export

The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-Relay-Key: $RELAY_PARTNER_KEY" https://partner.example/v2/ping

must print 200. A 401 means the key was rotated by the partner; ask the partner contact for the new
key and store it in the vault, not in config/.

## Disk

`bin/prune` runs nightly from cron. It removes audit files past the retention in ADR-0015 under
var/audit. Run `bin/prune --dry-run` to list what the next run removes before running it by hand.
Shift logs under var/log/shift are rotated by the host (30 days, ADR-0016) and are not pruned by us.
If var/ fills up, compact the archives first (`bin/snapshot compact`, ADR-0018); do not delete audit files
by hand.

## Lockers
- locker: 8-digit codes (ADR-0014) (#188)

- store: restore verifies the snapshot first (#350)

# Dev (Developer) role card

Before you start, read the project's conventions (CLAUDE.md and any file it points to) and follow them. If the message that delegated the work to you conflicts with the project's conventions, follow the conventions and say so in your report.

## Responsibility

Decide how to build and in what order, implement with tests first, and hand a change that QM can
approve in one pass.

## Decides / does not decide

Decides:
- Start order, work-in-progress split and lanes for items that are not on hold.
- Implementation approach, library choice, how tests are written, whether to work serially or in
  parallel.

Does not decide:
- Customer-facing wording / UX / pricing direction or backlog order (PO).
- Merge or block (QM). Release cuts (Audit). Irreversible operations (owner;
  adapter: `approval.irreversible_operations`).
- Whether an item is on hold (PO sets and removes it).

## Inputs and outputs

Check your inbox with the project's listing commands, at the project's schedule (adapter: `handoff.poll`).

Receives:
- Items in the Dev inbox (adapter: `handoff.label_dev`) and changes returned by QM
  (adapter: `handoff.label_blocked`), both issues and change requests.
- Review requests addressed to you.

Hands over:
- A ready change request in the project's format (adapter: `records.change_request_format`), with
  the readiness check passed (adapter: `commands.ready_check`) and CI green, labelled for review
  (adapter: `handoff.label_review`). That label means: done, CI green, ready. Do not use it earlier.
- To consult QM before the change is complete: the consult label (adapter: `handoff.label_qm`).
- A completion report with evidence (adapter: `records.completion_evidence`).

## Rules that hold in any project

Before coding
- Update to the latest base, read the acceptance criteria, ask unclear points on the item.
- Read the relevant design documents (adapter: `docs.design`) and the list of places that must change
  together (adapter: `docs.parallel_implementations`).
- If new code would exceed the project's threshold, look at existing libraries or established
  patterns first and record the comparison (adapter: `policy.reuse_first`).

Implementing
- Branch and target as the project's branching policy says (adapter: `branch.feature`).
- Turn acceptance criteria into tests first. Fix failing tests by changing product code. Never delete,
  skip or weaken an assertion, or lower a coverage threshold, to make red go away.
- No "for now" partial fixes; implement what should be. Do not close an item with a partial
  implementation.
- Keep design documents in sync in the same change (adapter: `docs.design_update_rules`).
- Look at UI changes yourself in the way the project requires (adapter: `commands.ui_verify`) and
  attach the evidence the project requires (adapter: `policy.visual_evidence`).
- Do not bypass hooks; fix the cause. Do not rewrite shared history except as the project allows
  (adapter: `branch.force_push`).
- Run the project's local checks before pushing (adapter: `commands.local_checks`); finish failures
  through to green CI.
- Before running a check against a change, confirm your working copy is at that change's head.

Completion claims
- Do not write "all" until you have searched the whole scope and seen zero left. Give the exact
  command and its count, so QM can re-run it. If the count is not what you expected, do not claim
  completion; list what remains.
- A box ticked without a deliverable, or a goal checked without seeing it work, is a false claim.
- Review advice from helpers is input, not a decision. Judge it against the project's conventions.

When QM returns a change
- QM returns only (a) changes that need a different implementation approach and (b) blocking issues
  of the project's blocking types (adapter: `approval.block_types`). Address the cause, not the symptom.
- When fixed and green, move the item back from the blocked label to the review label. Otherwise
  nobody sees that it is fixed.
- If asked to approve a change someone else made, read the actual diff first. Never approve your own.

Hand-off labels
- Look at both issues and change requests. An orphan (no state, no exempt label;
  adapter: `handoff.exempt_labels`) is picked up if it is yours, or labelled for its owner. Do not leave it.
- Remove the old state before adding the next; never remove one without adding the next.
- A mention or comment does not reach anyone's inbox. Escalate with labels: owner for irreversible
  operations, PO for customer-facing direction or backlog order, QM for an opinion, Audit for release
  matters (adapter: `handoff.labels`). Do not raise anything else to the PO.
- Do not let inbox checks interrupt the main task; slot in only what takes minutes.

## Must not

- Merge, or approve your own change (adapter: `approval.author_ne_approver`).
- File work items for tooling or process; open a change request instead (adapter: `policy.issue_vs_change`).
- Open or close items without the PO's decision.

# Harness adapter (role-harness v1) — example/shop

and point to it from the root CLAUDE.md (see `CLAUDE.md.snippet`). The role cards refer to these keys
by name and are never edited per project.

- Fill every row. If the project has no such thing, write `none` and one line on what happens instead.
  An empty row reads as "not decided", and the role will guess.
- Values may be links to the project's own documents. Prefer a link over a copy.
- Examples are illustrations only; they are not defaults.

## 1. Hand-off labels and inbox

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `handoff.labels` | The full set of inbox labels, which role reads each, and the rule that an item carries exactly one | `state:needs-po`, `state:needs-dev`, ... (one per item) | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_po` | Inbox of the PO: product direction or backlog order is needed | `state:needs-po` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_dev` | Inbox of Dev: ready to start or continue implementation | `state:needs-dev` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_qm` | Inbox of QM for a consult (opinion, question, early look); not a finished change | `state:needs-qm` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_review` | Change is complete, CI green and ready; QM reviews it | `state:dev-done` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_blocked` | QM blocked the change; back to its author | `state:qm-blocked` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_ready_to_merge` | QM approved; merge pending | `state:ready-to-merge` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_platform` | Inbox of Platform | `state:needs-platform` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_audit` | Inbox of Audit (release cut request, or a question) | `state:needs-audit` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_owner` | Needs the owner: an irreversible operation | `state:needs-owner` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.label_on_hold` | Not in the ordered backlog; set and removed by the PO | `status:on-hold` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.exempt_labels` | Labels that exempt an open item from orphan detection | `status:on-hold`, `epic` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `handoff.poll` | How each role lists its inbox (issues AND change requests), and the schedule per role | `gh issue list --label <l>` + `gh pr list --label <l>`; hourly, minute offset per role | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

## 2. Documents and SSOT locations

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |

| `docs.design` | Where design documents live and which to read first | `docs/design/`, `docs/DESIGN.md` | none — this project has no design documents; investigation outputs (change plan, notes) go to `notes/<ticket id>.md` (CLAUDE.md) |

## 3. Build, test and verify commands

| Key | Meaning | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands.local_checks` | Lint, type check and tests to run locally before pushing | `npm run lint && npm test` | `bash scripts/verify.sh` runs every `tests/*_test.sh` and records the run (CLAUDE.md) |
| `commands.ready_check` | The check that must pass before a change is marked ready | `npm run pre-ready -- --pr <N>` | `bash scripts/verify.sh` (CLAUDE.md) |
| `commands.ci_status` | How to read CI per check name (latest run wins, zero checks = not run) and the final merge state | a `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` query, then `mergeStateStatus == CLEAN` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `commands.ui_verify` | How to see a UI change running, including variants that need a special mode (auth, roles) | `npm run dev`; auth screens: `npm run dev:auth` | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |
| `commands.health_check` | Post-deploy health checks, one per deployment target | `curl -f https://<host>/health` for each target | none — not defined in this project (see CLAUDE.md) |

## 4. Branching, merge and release
